newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUCKLAND WARRIORS NOT FOR SALE, YET.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUCKLAND WARRIORS NOT FOR SALE, YET.

text.p: The Auckland Warriors Super League club is not for sale, but the consortium that wants to buy it for NZ$4 million is confident the Auckland Rugby League (ARL) will eventually see merit in the offer.

Former Kiwis coach Graham Lowe, along with former Kiwis test forward Dean Lonergan and businessman Malcolm Boyle, said on Thursday they were prepared to make a formal bid of NZ$4 million (US$2.6 million) to buy the Warriors.
They were prevented from tabling the offer at a meeting of ARL clubs on Wednesday before the ARL decided not to sell their interest in the Super League franchise.
"Given time to carefully consider our bid, I am confident the Auckland Rugby League will see a great deal in merit in what we are offering," Lowe said.
"Personally, I am not convinced the ARL clubs are aware of just how much of a financial mess the Warriors have become and just what is at stake here.
"We will bring the necessary expertise needed to ensure the Warriors are competently managed and can match it with any league club in the world.
"I'm confident the Warriors can become the most powerful club in the game," he added.
The Warriors are currently languishing at the bottom of the Super League competition table.

The consortium members said they believed the ARL would have to sell the Warriors eventually because it was not in the business of managing risk, which was what running an enterprise like the Warriors was about.
"Super League is not going to go on and keep funding and supporting the Warriors," Boyle said.
"Also, they badly need an injection of expertise and experience that people like Dean Lonergan and Graham Lowe can bring to the table."
Auckland Warriors chief executive Bill MacGowan said the vote against the sale was overwhelming, with only one dissenter, but he agreed the issue was not dead.
"But if the ARL wants to sell the Warriors, it needs to go to the market," he said.
MacGowan said it would be "naive" to think the ARL would consider just one offer.
The Warriors' financial situation improved earlier this week after Super League agreed to give the ARL an unsecured loan.
The size of the loan has not been made public, but the Warriors already owe Super League NZ$1.1 million and need further money to get them through to next season.
